title: Personal repair list and question-level analysis
subject: English Language
source: Seeded from english-language/y11 lessons 40, 41, 42, 52, 53, 54 (Personal repair list and question-level analysis (pupil PDF))
intro: Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: in the portal response box, rewrite your mock Q3 or Q6 answer opening (one paragraph) so it weaves language, structure and effect. Starter: 'The writer uses ... to ...; this ...'
questions.a: One paragraph analysing a language choice and a structural feature, each with a clear effect on the reader.
questions.model: Before: 'The writer uses a simile. It is effective.' After: 'The writer personifies the sea as a judge, "weighing us", which makes the passengers seem powerless; structurally, the short sentence "Nobody spoke." then stops the reader, so the silence itself becomes tense.'

questions.q: add your top three repairs to your repair list with dates.
questions.a: Three repairs, each with a gap, cause, task and date.

questions.q: rehearse a 1-mark and a 2-mark answer from the mock in under one minute each.
Fill in your question-level analysis and circle your three biggest losses.
questions.a: Marks recorded and three losses identified with causes.
questions.model: Teacher models with an anonymous paper: 'Q3 5/10: named a simile, no effect. Q7 6/15: Text Two barely used. Section C 14/30: unfinished. Biggest gains: Q7 and Section C.'

questions.q: Name the cause of each of your three losses (misread, timing, skill, accuracy).

questions.a: B) gap, cause, task and date

questions.q: Answer the ponder in one sentence.
questions.a: Answers vary, e.g. the short questions and Q7 comparison.

questions.q: in the portal response box, rewrite your weakest mock Q7 or Q8 paragraph using today's models. Starter (Q7): 'Both writers present..., although...' or (Q8): 'If you are...'
questions.a: A repaired paragraph: integrated comparison with methods (Q7), or transformed ideas for audience and purpose (Q8).
questions.model: Q7 before: 'Text One is scared. Text Two gives advice.' After: 'Both writers present the sea as beyond human control, although the memoir's writer is terrified while the letter-writer is amused; the first-person present moment draws us into fear, whereas the imperatives of Text Two keep a confident distance.'

questions.q: highlight every comparative connective (Q7) or transformed idea (Q8).
write a conclusion sentence that synthesises both texts.
questions.a: For example: Ultimately, both writers suggest that the sea teaches humility, though only one learns it through fear.

questions.q: Transform this text idea into advice for a Year 9 audience: 'the ordinary safety I had been so keen to escape'.
questions.a: For example: You may feel homesick on your first trip; that feeling shows how much home matters, and it passes.
questions.model: Idea: the writer missed home's safety. Audience: Year 9. Purpose: advise. Transform: 'Homesickness is normal: it shows what home gives you, and it fades within days.'

questions.q: Write the P and E of a Q7 paragraph on the writers' attitudes to travel.
questions.a: P: both value what travel teaches, although... E: one short quotation from each text.
A) both texts in every paragraph

questions.q: in the portal response box, write your personal revision plan to 24 May (one line a week) and one Section C five-line plan for 'Describe a market as it closes for the night.' Starter: 'Week of 15 Mar: ...'
questions.a: A dated weekly plan linked to repairs, and a controlled five-line plan.
questions.model: Week of 15 Mar: Q7 repair (two paragraphs). Week of 22 Mar: Section B timed. Week of 31 Mar: Section C timed. Week of 5 Apr: Section A timed. Week of 12 Apr: full paper. Week of 19 Apr: repair weakest section. Then: weekly timed section and error log review to 24 May. | Plan: wide square; stalls folding; one lantern; smells fading; empty, quiet.
